explanation:
The `pthread_attr_setschedparam()` and `pthread_attr_getschedparam()` functions are used to manage the scheduling parameters associated with a POSIX thread attributes object (`pthread_attr_t`). These parameters dictate the scheduling priority of any new thread created using the modified attribute object.

`pthread_attr_setschedparam()` takes two arguments: a pointer to the attribute object (`attr`) and a constant pointer to a `struct sched_param` (`param`). The `struct sched_param` currently supports a single member, `int sched_priority`, which specifies the desired scheduling priority for the new thread. The permissible range for `sched_priority` depends on the scheduling policy defined in the attribute object (which can be set using `pthread_attr_setschedpolicy(3)`).

`pthread_attr_getschedparam()` retrieves the currently stored scheduling parameters from the attribute object (`attr`) and stores them in the buffer pointed to by `param`.

Crucially, for the priority set by `pthread_attr_setschedparam()` to be honored during thread creation via `pthread_create(3)`, the calling program must explicitly set the inherit-scheduler attribute to `PTHREAD_EXPLICIT_SCHED` using `pthread_attr_setinheritsched(3)`. If the inherit attribute is left at the default (`PTHREAD_INHERIT_SCHED`), the new thread inherits the scheduler parameters (policy and priority) of the parent thread, ignoring the settings in the attributes object.

Both functions return 0 upon successful completion. On error, a non-zero error number is returned, such as `EINVAL` if the priority specified is outside the range permitted by the currently active scheduling policy (for `setschedparam`).
keywords: pthread_attr_setschedparam, pthread_attr_getschedparam, sched_param, thread attributes, scheduling priority, POSIX threads, PTHREAD_EXPLICIT_SCHED, real-time scheduling, libpthread
example_explanation: This code initializes a thread attributes object, sets its policy to SCHED_RR and enables explicit scheduling, then uses `pthread_attr_setschedparam` to assign a middle-range real-time priority, and finally verifies the stored value using `pthread_attr_getschedparam`.
